I'm exploring part-time data science and analytics work outside my full-time role, and I'm doing that by having conversations first, not by selling a package.

## Who I want to talk to

Organizations, in any industry, that have data — in spreadsheets, an ERP, a CRM, or wherever it lives — but no dedicated data analyst or data scientist to make sense of it. That's the situation I know best, from the outside now and the inside for years: working out which decisions actually matter, what the data can and can't say, and building the first useful analysis, automation, or tool.

## What I bring

- **Decision-focused analytics.** Statistics and machine learning applied to a real decision, not analysis for its own sake: descriptive, diagnostic, predictive, and prescriptive work, in that order of maturity.
- **Automation over repetition.** Replacing manual, spreadsheet-driven reporting with scripted, reproducible analysis in Python, R, or SQL.
- **Interactive tools, not static reports.** Dashboards and small applications (Streamlit, R Shiny) that let people explore a question instead of reading a slide.
- **Judgment on the method.** Knowing when a simple baseline is enough and when causal inference, forecasting, or a more advanced model earns its complexity.

I've applied this in healthcare — forecasting, causal inference, decision support — and I publish projects outside healthcare as they're finished, so the work here isn't tied to one industry.

## Where things stand

I'm not taking paid engagements yet. I'm validating whether part-time consulting is a good fit for me and a good fit for the organizations I'd want to work with, before I build anything to sell. If you're open to a 20-minute conversation about how your organization uses data today, I'd genuinely value it — no pitch, no follow-up sales email.
